claim.statement: V3.19 is validated for the implemented Unix-socket IPC and daemon/watch surfaces on macOS and Linux: the full Rust test suite passes on the macOS host and in a disposable Debian Linux container, including socket permissions, frame protocol, concurrent writers, daemon lifecycle, watcher subprocesses, hook fetch, watch loop, and restart/session recovery tests.

evidence.summary: macOS host `cargo test` passed 21 unit tests and 29 integration tests. Linux container `cargo test` passed the same suite after fixing timeout handling to kill watcher process groups, validating the cross-platform IPC/process behavior on Debian arm64.

information_depth.rationale: The Linux run exercised the same compiled integration suite and caught a process-group timeout bug that was fixed and revalidated.

claim.statement: Watcher timeout enforcement now kills the watcher process group, not only the shell wrapper, so child processes cannot keep stdout/stderr pipes open and delay timeout completion on Linux.

evidence.summary: The first Linux matrix run failed `watcher_timeout_and_cost_caps_are_enforced` because a child `sleep` outlived the killed shell. The implementation was changed to use `CommandExt::process_group(0)` and `killpg(..., SIGKILL)`; the Linux rerun passed.

information_depth.rationale: This is direct regression evidence from the platform matrix.
